Overview:

Get ready to put your HR knowledge to the ultimate test! HRiday - The HR and People’s Club of GIM presents InQuizitive 2025-26, a national-level HR quiz competition. Compete with the brightest minds across the country, showcase your expertise in HR concepts, and win exciting prizes. Don’t miss the chance to prove your mettle in this thrilling battle of wits! This isn't just a quiz; it's a leadership odyssey. Sharpen your mind, unlock potential, and lead your organization to a brighter future. Join InQuizitive!

General Guidelines:

Competition Structure: Quiz

Round 1:

- Answer 10 multiple-choice questions in 10 minutes to test your knowledge of comprehensive people management concepts and unravel the secrets of leadership with an HR approach.

Round 2:

General Guidelines:

  • Teams can consist of 1 to 4 members.
  • Cross Functional/Course teams are allowed (team members can be from any specialization).

Round 1 – Solution Submission (Case Analysis):

  • The team will analyze the detailed case study uploaded on the platform.
  • The task is to answer the questions provided at the end of the case study document.
  • Responses must be structured into a presentation of 4-5 slide presentation (excluding the introduction and appendix).
  • The presentation can be submitted in PPTX or PDF format. Links to online presentations will not be accepted)
  • Top 10 teams will be shortlisted for Round 2.
  • Nomenclature for submission: "Team Name"_"College Name"_GIM_Samiksha

Round 2 – Presentation Round (Final Round):

  • The top 10 teams from Round 1 will advance to the Final Round.
  • Each shortlisted team will present its Round 1 solution to the judge in a live online session.
  • Presentations will be evaluated on accuracy, communication, and clarity of thought, originality and innovative thinking, use of data-driven insights, ethical sensitivity, and presentation skills.
  • A Q&A round will follow each presentation, during which the judge will challenge the team's ideas and explore the reasoning behind the proposed solution.
  • The winning team will be announced after the final evaluation.

Rules and Regulations:

Round 1 – Solution Submission

  • Case study goes live: 19th September 2026
  • Deadline for presentation submission: 22nd September 2026, 23:59 PM
  • The presentation must consist of 4–5 slides, covering the team's approach to the questions in a concise and structured manner. The introduction and appendix are excluded from the slide count.
  • Format: PPTX or PDF only.
  • Nomenclature for submission: "Team Name"_"College Name"_GIM_Samiksha

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Communication and clarity of thought
  • Originality and innovative thinking
  • Use of data-driven insights from the case
  • Ethical sensitivity in proposed solutions

Round 2 - Presentation Round (Final Round)

  • Final round will take place on 26th September 2026
  • Shortlisted teams will be informed via email with further instructions.
  • Each team will present their Round 1 solution to the judge in an online live session via a MS Teams Meeting (link will be shared with all finalists).

General Rules:

  • Ensure timely submission; late entries will not be accepted.
  • Participants are expected to maintain a respectful and professional approach throughout the event.
  • Participants must comply with all instructions communicated by the organisers during the competition.

data.title: The Nation Builders 2026
data.details:
Overview

A National Article Writing Competition | Teachers’ Day Edition

Organised by: Youthisthan Foundation
Eligibility: 14 years and above
Mode: Online
Category: Article Writing / Creative Writing / Education
Language: English
Word Limit: Up to 1200 words

About the Competition

Some people teach lessons. Some shape lives. Educators shape nations.

The Nation Builders 2026 is a national-level article writing competition organised by Youthisthan Foundation as a special Teachers’ Day Edition.

The competition invites young writers, students, educators, professionals, and thoughtful individuals to share their perspectives on education, teachers, students, schools, parents, technology, Artificial Intelligence, and the future of learning.

This is a platform to go beyond conventional writing and ask meaningful questions:

What should education look like tomorrow?
What should change in our classrooms?
What role will teachers play in an AI-powered world?
How can education help build a better India?

Your article could become part of a larger conversation about the people and ideas shaping the future of education.

Think. Question. Write. Inspire.

Who Can Participate?

The competition is open to anyone aged 14 years and above.

We welcome participation from:

  • School students
  • College and university students
  • Teachers and educators
  • Researchers
  • Professionals
  • Aspiring writers
  • Education enthusiasts
  • Young thinkers and changemakers

You do not need to be a professional writer. You simply need an idea worth expressing.

What Can You Write About?

Participants can explore contemporary questions and perspectives related to:

  • The changing role of teachers
  • The future of education in India
  • Education and nation-building
  • Students and the changing learning environment
  • Artificial Intelligence and education
  • Technology in classrooms
  • Creativity and critical thinking
  • Examination and learning culture
  • The role of parents and schools
  • Inclusive and meaningful education
  • Education beyond academics
  • Preparing learners for the future

Participants are encouraged to develop their own perspective rather than simply presenting generic information.

Submission Guidelines

  • The article must be original work.
  • Maximum word limit: 1200 words.
  • Entries must be submitted in English.
  • Participants can submit one article.
  • The article should be relevant to the broad theme of education, teachers, and nation-building.
  • Personal experiences, observations, and original ideas are encouraged.
  • Plagiarism is strictly prohibited.
  • Previously published articles should not be submitted.
  • Participants are expected to submit their own work and ideas.

Evaluation Criteria

Entries will be evaluated on:

  • Originality of Thought: Does the article present an interesting or distinctive perspective?
  • Relevance & Depth: Does it meaningfully address the chosen subject?
  • Creativity & Insight: Does the writer go beyond conventional arguments?
  • Clarity & Expression: Is the writing clear, engaging, and well structured?
  • Overall Impact: Does the article leave the reader with something to think about?

What Do You Get?

Outstanding entries can receive:

  • Cash Prizes
  • Premium Mementos
  • Certificates
  • LinkedIn-Verified Certificate
  • Publication Opportunities
  • Recognition on Youthisthan Foundation's platforms

The latest official promotion specifically highlights cash prizes, premium mementos, LinkedIn-verified certificates, and publication opportunities.

Selected articles may also become part of the growing body of education-focused writing associated with The Nation Builders. Previous editions have featured winning and selected articles on the Youthisthan Foundation website and social platforms.

Important Dates

  • Registration Closes: 14 September 2026
  • Article Submission: 20 September 2026
  • Results: 5 October 2026

Why Participate?

This is not simply a competition to add another certificate to your profile.

It is an opportunity to:

  • Develop and showcase your writing
  • Express your perspective on education
  • Engage with important questions facing learners and educators
  • Build your writing portfolio
  • Gain recognition at a national platform
  • Get an opportunity for publication
  • Contribute to a wider conversation about India's educational future

Your words can honour those who build our future.

Submission Details

Submission link will be shared on your registered email id within 24 hours after registration. The submission link is also available on the official website of Youthisthan Foundation www.youthisthanfoundation.org/the-nation-builders

For more details visit the official website or write at info@youthisthanfoundation.org

About Youthisthan Foundation

Youthisthan Foundation is a nonprofit organisation working to create opportunities for learning, youth engagement, creative expression, and social impact.

Its initiatives include national competitions, educational programmes, knowledge platforms, and campaigns encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, leadership, and civic engagement.

For The Youth For The Nation

The Nation Builders 2026 is a national-level article writing competition by Youthisthan Foundation, presented as a special Teachers’ Day Edition. Open to participants aged 14+, the competition invites original perspectives on teachers, education, students, technology, AI, and the future of learning. Submit an article of up to 1200 words and get an opportunity to earn national recognition, certificates, premium mementos, publication opportunities, and more. Think. Question. Write. Inspire.

Your Ideas Can Shape the Future of Education.

Stages:

Round 1: Fit for Investment (Quiz):

  • Platform: Live on Unstop
  • Dates: 14th Sep (00:00) – 22nd Sep (23:59)

  • Time: 10 minutes
  • Scoring: +1 per correct answer (maximum 20 points)
  • Eligibility: Open to all registered teams; one attempt per team

  • Platform: Live on Unstop
  • Dates: 23rd Sep (00:00) – 1st Oct (23:59)

Teams submit a 5-slide Pitch Deck:

  • Slide 1 - Executive Summary & Fund Allocation
  • Slide 2 - Market Opportunity analysis considering the trends in the market and competitor analysis using Data Visualization and analysis
  • Slide 3 - Risk Assessment, Financial assessment (Top 3 business/market risks and proposed mitigation and investment strategies)

Guidelines:

  • The decision of the organizers and judges will be final and binding on all participating teams.
  • By registering, all participants agree to be bound by these rules and any additional terms communicated during the competition.

data.title: Commercio Artikel - Article Writing Competition
data.details:
An acronym for Buy Low And Sell High, BLASH is the International Trade Club at IIFT. It is one of the oldest student-driven clubs in the college and has a track record of attracting the highest membership in all student batches to date. The club aims to bring together people who wish to make a career in Trade and International Business and provide a platform to interact and learn dimensions of international trade beyond the regular classroom learning, thereby broadening their horizons. BLASH is also the focal point of external engagement with organizations from the domains of Commodity Trading, International Logistics, Structured Trade Finance, and related spheres.

Every year the student body at IIFT organizes Trade Winds: International Business Conclave to gain insights from pre-eminent business leaders from diverse industries so as to polish our business outlook. The theme for Trade Winds 2026 is “Reglobalization: Navigating Trade in a Changing World”.

Under the aegis of Trade Winds, BLASH organises the National Trade Summit and hosts Commercio Artikel, a national-level article writing competition that allows students to express their views on recent trade developments and their take on the future. To participate, students are required to submit an article (Minimum 800 words) on international trade-related topics. The sub-theme for the National Trade Summit is "The Weaponization of Trade: Export Controls and the Rise of Economic Security"

Some of the suggested topics for reference are:

  • The Semiconductor Divide: Can Emerging Economies Compete in an Era of High-Tech Export Controls?
  • ​The Resurgence of Industrial Policy: Balancing Domestic Economic Security with the Need for Global Market Access.
  • ​Beyond the Dollar: How Financial Statecraft and Sanctions are Reshaping Cross-Border Trade Mechanisms.
  • ​The New Resource War: The Race to Secure Critical Tech and Rare Earth Minerals in a Fragmented Global Market.
  • ​Alliances Over Economics: How Geopolitical Partnerships are Redefining Traditional Free Trade Blocs.

Kindly note that the above topics are suggestive in nature. Best articles will be published in the annual magazine of BLASH, IIFT Delhi during TradeWinds 2026. This is your chance to show your analysis and highlight your opinions on matters concerning international trade. Time to start researching and penning down your thoughts right away. Exciting cash prizes are in store for winners!

Guidelines:

  • Team formation rules: Individual or team of 2
  • Word Limit: 800-1200 words
  • Font: Times New Roman and Font size must be 12
  • The naming convention of the document: TeamName_CollegeName
  • All the articles in Doc (Word) format should be uploaded to this portal
  • The article should be original work and references must be cited wherever necessary.
  • Relevant Graphs or data can be added to the article, but they need to be created not snipped.

Rules:

  • Plagiarism will lead to disqualification
  • Deadlines are to be strictly followed
  • Cash prizes worth Rs. 8000 for the top three submissions

data.title: Strategos 2026: Article Writing Competition
data.details:
Socrates, the Consulting and Strategy Club of IIFT Delhi, proudly presents the 2026 edition of its flagship Article Writing Competition – Strategos.

At Socrates, we work to bridge the gap between B-school students and the consulting world. The club focuses on breaking down the complexities of consulting, offering a deeper understanding of the industry, its challenges, and the skillsets it demands. Each year, the IIFT community hosts Trade Winds: The International Business Conclave, a forum where industry stalwarts share their wisdom and perspectives, enriching student learning.

As part of Trade Winds, Socrates organizes Strategos, a pan-India article writing contest that provides students a chance to showcase original thought, critical insights, and bold perspectives. The theme for Trade Winds 2026 is “Reglobalization: Navigating Trade in a Changing World”. We invite students from campuses across the country to pen down their views and contribute to meaningful discourse on the future of trade, strategy, and digital transformation. 

Prizes & Recognition:

  • Top 3 articles will receive cash prizes worth INR 8000/-.
  • Top 5 articles will be published in the annual magazine of Socrates.

Participants need to build upon the theme and write an article on any of the following topics:

Topics:

  • The Geography of Growth: Strategic Market Selection in an Increasingly Fragmented Global Economy
  • Building Resilient Advantage: Designing Operating Models for Growth Under Geopolitical Uncertainty
  • Capital Allocation Under Uncertainty: Balancing Growth Opportunities Against Geopolitical Risk
  • The Capability Imperative: Building Competitive Advantage in a World of Strategic Interdependence

The article should emphasize the author's opinion and ideas. Please note that plagiarism of any kind will lead to disqualification.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Structure and flow of the article
  • Depth and originality of analysis
  • Use of data, graphs, and visual representation
  • Clarity of opinion and argumentation

Guidelines:

  • Word Limit: 800-1200 words
  • Font: Times New Roman (size - 12)
  • Use of graphs, figures, tables & other modes of data representation would fetch brownie points

data.title: Moneyball: The Football Auction (Interface 2026)
data.details:
About the Event:

Moneyball: The Football Auction is an immersive football management and auction simulation that challenges participants to build and strengthen their teams through strategic bidding, squad planning, match simulation, and player negotiations. Participants will compete in teams, combining football knowledge, strategic thinking, decision-making, and negotiation skills in a competitive environment.

Event Flow:

Pre-Fest Round: Football Quiz (Online Round):

The event begins with a fast-paced online quiz hosted on Unstop, designed to assess participants' knowledge of general knowledge and recent footballing events.

  • The quiz will be conducted online on Unstop.
  • The quiz will consist of 35 questions.
  • The duration of the quiz will be 12 minutes.
  • Only the Team Leader will have access to the quiz on behalf of the team.
  • Participants will be allowed to modify their answers before final submission.
  • The top 10 teams based on their performance in the quiz will qualify for the next round.

Bid Maestro (On-Campus Round):

The shortlisted teams will participate in Bid Maestro, the core football auction round. Each team will build its squad through a competitive auction while strategically managing its allocated purse.

Teams will be required to build a squad of at least 11 players, including:

  • 1–2 Goalkeepers
  • 3–5 Defenders
  • 2–4 Midfielders
  • 2–4 Forwards

The objective of this round is to maximize the overall strength of the team while efficiently utilizing the allocated purse.

  • Every player will have an associated strength based on which teams will bid for them.
  • Once the squads are formed, matches will be simulated on FIFA in a round-robin format.
  • Based on the simulation results, teams will be ranked from 1 to 10.
  • Teams ranked 1–4 will be classified as the Top 4, while teams ranked 5–10 will form the Bottom 6.

Transfer Market:

The Top 4 teams will get an opportunity to further strengthen their squads by acquiring players from the Bottom 6 teams using their remaining purse.

Teams will be required to:

  • Select up to 3 preferred players they wish to acquire from players released by the Bottom 6 teams.
  • Negotiate with the respective player managers through a classified negotiation process.
  • Finalize each negotiation within 3 minutes.

After the transfer market, the modified squads of the Top 4 teams will be simulated again on FIFA to determine the final standings and the champions.

The Best Negotiator Award will be awarded to the team from the Bottom 6 that has the maximum purse remaining at the end of the negotiation process.

Additional Rules:

  • Teams must have a minimum of 1 member and a maximum of 5 members.
  • The Team Leader will represent the team during the bidding process.
  • Only the Team Leader can raise their hand and place bids on behalf of the team.
  • Teams must bring their laptops for the event.

data.title: Ops Rewire
data.details:
Overview

OPUS presents OpsRewire, a two-round operations competition designed to test your operational acumen, analytical thinking, and strategic decision-making.

Step into the shoes of decision-makers at a global electric vehicle manufacturer facing a critical operations dilemma:

Should the company continue with local manufacturing, shift towards importing and assembling vehicles, or adopt a hybrid model?

Analyse the trade-offs, work with the available data, and build a recommendation that balances cost, capacity, localisation, supplier dependence, lead times, inventory, scalability, and long-term sustainability.

Round 1 — Quiz

  • An online quiz testing your understanding of operations, operational strategy, and decision-making.
  • 20 questions | 15 minutes
  • One member from each team must attempt the quiz.
  • Quiz closes: 15 September, EOD
  • Top-performing teams will advance to Round 2.

Round 2 — Case Presentation

Shortlisted teams will receive the case and develop their solution.

  • Analyse the business problem and evaluate the available alternatives.
  • Present your findings and strategic recommendation in a 5-slide presentation.
  • Submission window: 16th–20th September
  • Submission: Online via Unstop

Team Details

  • Team Size: 2–4 members
  • Platform: Unstop

Prizes

  • Prize Pool: ₹3,000
